methods.what: Condition for the square root $\sqrt{-ss+sz-qq/4}$ to be real gives $s$ between the roots $\frac{z\pm\sqrt{zz-qq}}{2}$
Solving for the boundary point where the limits coincide: $z=t+qq/4t$
Case split of the $s$-integration range according to $z \gtrless t+qq/4t$
Decomposition of the double integral $u$ into a part $P$ plus an integral over the full root interval
Chain of inequalities verifying $2(z-t) > z-\sqrt{zz-qq}$ for $z>t+qq/4t$
Analogous integral and limits with $xx/(\alpha\alpha pp)$ in place of $qq$
